title: KYE AI-Tell Lexicon — example instance
description: Illustrative instance showing all three tell dimensions: a phrase and a word (scored, with severities and an allow_context whitelist), and a punctuation tell (not scored — enforced net-new-strict on the change-set). surface_corpus shows how the scanned population is DECLARED rather than enumerated by each scanner.

scoring.note: weighted hit = severity weight; scored tells are judged per entity, so there is no site-wide total to bank.

phrases.why: throat-clearing filler opener — the canonical AI intro
chatbot narration; copy shows, doesn't announce

words.why: AI adjective; rarely true, never specific

surface_corpus.rationale: The page graph already declares which pages are buyer-facing, so both the voice scanner and the clarity scorer resolve one answer instead of each hand-typing a surface list and walking it non-recursively.

excluded.reason: A generated catalogue table, not authored prose; a generator's rows are neither credited nor penalised.

applies_to.rationale: The authored sources of the buyer-facing corpus; generated output is excluded so one edit is counted once.

punctuation.why: The em-dash is the most recognisable punctuation fingerprint of machine-authored prose. The tell is the character used as the DEFAULT clause separator, where a comma, a colon or a rewritten sentence would carry the meaning.

enforcement.basis: Enforceable at t=0 with no stored number: the gate diffs the change-set's own range and refuses a source file that gained an occurrence. A per-page count would be a ratchet.

migration.owed: The pre-existing population is declared once here, never as one rubber-stamped row per page.

measured_at_declaration.command: count U+2014 in the visible prose of every buyer-facing page the corpus resolves
measured_at_declaration.finding: Measured across the declared corpus at declaration time; the figure lives on the registry row, not here.
